question: At which place was India’s first Grass Conservatory launched by the Research Wing of the Uttarakhand Forest Department in November 2021?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Ranikhet__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's first ‘grass conservatory’ **spread over an area of two acres was inaugurated at **Ranikhet in Almora district**. 
 
• Funded under the Central Government's CAMPA scheme, the conservatory was developed in three years by the research wing of Uttarakhand Forest Department, Chief Conservator of Forest (research) Sanjiv Chaturvedi said.
 
• Around **90 different grass species** of significant scientific, ecological, medicinal, and cultural import have been grown in the conservation area.
 
• The project aims to **create awareness about the importance of grass species, promote their conservation, and facilitate research in the field**.
 
• The initiative assumes importance as it has been proved in the latest research that **grasslands are more effective in ‘carbon sequestration’ than forest land**.
 
• It is also important because grasslands are facing various types of threats and their area is shrinking, endangering an entire ecosystem of insects, birds, and mammals dependent on them. 
 
• Grasses are economically the most important of all flowering plants because of their nutritious grain and soil-forming function.
 
• The conservation area has **seven different categories of grass species** including those that are known for their aromatic, medicinal, fodder, ornamental, agricultural, and religious uses. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Central Government's Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) scheme, as established under the CAMPA Act of 2016.
 
• It is an Indian conservation initiative aimed at promoting afforestation and regeneration activities as a way of compensating for forest land diverted to non-forest uses.
 
• The funds emerging from this scheme are sourced from payments made by user agencies (such as mining companies or infrastructure developers), who are utilizing forest land for non-forest purposes.
 
• These funds are meant to mitigate environmental impacts by financing the protection and rehabilitation of forest ecosystems across the country.
 
• State CAMPA authorities receive 90% of the collections, with the National CAMPA retaining the balance.
 
• The funds are used to nurture new forests, protect existing ones, manage wildlife, provide infrastructure and facilities for forest protection, improve livelihood options for communities dependent on forests, and for research and training related to afforestation and biodiversity conservation.
 
• This scheme recognizes the ecological and environmental costs associated with diverting forest lands for industrial or infrastructural projects and ensures restorative justice through the rejuvenation of forest resources, biodiversity conservation, and supporting livelihoods that are dependent on forests.
